children: New Delhi, Oct. 7 -- Deepa Jewellers share price jumped over 13% on Wednesday, bucking the broader market sell-off as Indian equities came under pressure after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised the policy rate by 25 basis points. Rate-sensitive sectors bore the brunt of the decline amid persistent inflationary pressures stemming from the Middle East conflict, prompting central banks globally to reassess their monetary policy stance.
However, Deepa Jewellers shares remained firmly in the green and were up around 37% from their IPO price, extending the strong gains seen since its market debut earlier this month.

The stock's rally comes shortly after the company reported strong Q1 FY27 financial results, with double-digit growth in revenue, EBITDA and net profit. While higher operating expenses led to a marginal contraction in EBITDA margin, the B2B jewellery processor continued to maintain its strong growth momentum following its stellar stock market debut.
Deepa Jewellers' net profit rose 27.01% year-on-year to Rs.26.76 crore in the quarter ended June 2026, compared with Rs.21.07 crore in the corresponding quarter a year ago.
Revenue from operations increased 39.04% to Rs.431.11 crore from Rs.310.06 crore in Q1 FY26.
EBITDA rose 34.02% YoY to Rs.38.68 crore, compared with Rs.28.86 crore a year earlier. However, EBITDA margin moderated to 8.97% from 9.31%, a contraction of 34 basis points.

The company operates in the organised B2B designer, processor and supplier segment of India's gems and jewellery industry. The sector is witnessing a shift towards hallmarked jewellery and organised players, which could benefit high-volume B2B suppliers as national and regional jewellery chains expand their retail footprint.

Deepa Jewellers made a strong debut on the exchanges on 8 September. On the BSE, the stock opened at Rs.221.05, a 24.88% premium to its IPO price of Rs.177, before ending the session at Rs.194.30, up 9.77%.
On the NSE, the stock listed at Rs.221, gaining 24.85% over the issue price, and closed at Rs.194.37, up 9.81%.

The company's Rs.460-crore IPO was subscribed nearly 43 times on the final day of bidding. The issue had a price band of Rs.168-177 per share and comprised a fresh issue of shares worth up to Rs.250 crore and an offer for sale of more than 1.18 crore shares.

The company plans to use proceeds from the fresh issue to fund long-term working capital requirements, including procurement, maintenance and scaling up of inventory, besides general corporate purposes.

Incorporated in 2016, Deepa Jewellers is an organised B2B designer, processor and supplier of hallmarked gold jewellery, with operations primarily across Telangana, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala. It designs, processes and sells a wide range of jewellery through an outsourced manufacturing model supported by a network of karigars.
